title: Expert upcycling symmetry-breaking View code
hypothesis: A small child-specific Mirror code breaks duplicated-expert symmetry and recovers child functions with fewer bytes and calibration examples than full continued pretraining, while beating random perturbation controls.
physical_object: one duplicated parent linear expert shared by child roles
mirror_coordinate: scalar coefficient over a shared learned residual direction
logical_multiplicity: eight child experts from one parent expert

development.selection_metric: heldout output nRMSE, payload bytes, calibration examples, optimizer updates and active compute

fresh.reason: exact native low-rank alias is assessed before fresh access

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: Heldout child nRMSE <=0.02 with >=25% fewer complete bytes than independent children, fewer updates/examples than CPT, and improvement beyond same-size native LoRA and random perturbation controls.
failure_gate: FAIL for Mirror-specific value if native LoRA exactly aliases the code or the code misses task quality; record learning efficiency separately from capacity.
boundaries: Synthetic linear child tasks only; no trained MoE pretraining, router quality, or language-model claim.
The shared basis is fit using training child identities only; heldout codes use calibration examples only.
Equal update counts are not capacity evidence; no capacity claim is made.
